analysis:
Examined the split of ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.currentStatus into a private liveDecision plus two public entry points, the new summary(removalAuthorization:) parameter, the DoctorRunner caller and the new docs paragraph (provider-authorization.md head 92-106).

liveDecision (head 44-58) keeps the base process-identity, coordinator-URL, finite-time, writtenAt<=10s, receivedAt>=startedAt, online and protocolVersion==1 checks. It drops only the receivedAt age check.

currentStatus (head 10-22) re-adds now-receivedAt<=snapshotMaxAge, so its behavior is identical to base. displayedStatus (head 28-40) also accepts an older receipt while hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization(now) holds; none/legacy decisions keep the 10s window.

summary (head 76-85) gives positive MDM-removal advice only when removalAuthorization equals the displayed authorization and removalReady holds. That decision comes from the strict currentStatus.

DoctorRunner (head 37-38, 78-79) computes the displayed and strict decisions from the same state and the same now. A late, unexpired lease can therefore still show 'App Attest authorizes this connection'. It can also suppress the AttestationReadiness and MDM-enrollment hints (base 67, 108). Both effects are local, read-only guidance. Per TB-011 and TB-002, doctor verdicts and local snapshots are not trust evidence. The coordinator's final handoff and EvaluateAuthorization stay authoritative, so this is not a serving, encryption or billing regression.

The TB-011 requirement that removal guidance needs a fresh current coordinator decision is preserved by the strict path. A delayed revocation could be masked only in the display, bounded by the lease's expires_at. Removal advice still fails closed.

Integration should confirm two things in other batches:
- The `darkbloom status` caller passes currentProviderAuthorization, not the displayed value, as removalAuthorization.
- UnenrollCommand+KeepServing still calls currentProviderAuthorization, as documented at head 105-106, and does not call displayedProviderAuthorization.

The changed summary signature forces every caller to be updated, which reduces the risk of a missed caller. No threat-model update appears required beyond optionally noting that display leases may outlast the 10s receipt window.
